questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 1 • Q1
questions.text: What kind of place is your hometown?

collocations.d: people know and support each other

examples.t: My hometown is quite peaceful, with friendly neighbours and decent local facilities.
It’s a medium-sized city with a lively centre, but the suburbs are calm.
Overall, it’s a comfortable place to live because transport is convenient.

gapFilling.prompt: My hometown has a ______ atmosphere, so it’s easy to relax there.
It’s a ______-knit community where people help each other.
The city has well-developed ______ such as transport and parks.

choices: an area outside the city centre

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence describing your hometown.
tips: Add one detail: transport, parks, people

samples.naturalSimple9: My hometown is a fairly calm place with a friendly atmosphere. It’s not huge, but it has the facilities people need, like parks and good transport. Overall, it feels comfortable and safe.
samples.advancedAcademic9: My hometown is a mid-sized urban area with a balanced lifestyle. It offers well-developed facilities and a strong sense of community, which makes daily life convenient. Overall, it’s a practical place to live with a pleasant atmosphere.
samples.fluentStory9: My hometown feels like a place that knows you. I grew up in a quiet neighbourhood where neighbours greeted each other and parks were always full in the evenings. Even now, when I visit, the atmosphere instantly makes me feel at home.

questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 1 • Q2
questions.text: Are there many trees or parks in your area?

collocations.d: roads with trees on both sides

vocab.d: plants and trees in an area
cool area out of the sun
keeping a place clean and in good condition

examples.t: Yes, there are a few parks within walking distance, so people go there to relax.
Not many, but the main park is well-maintained and has plenty of trees.
Tree-lined streets make the neighbourhood feel fresher in summer.

gapFilling.prompt: There’s a park ______ walking distance from my house.
The streets are ______-lined, which looks beautiful in spring.
I go there to ______ after work.

choices: a cool place out of the sun
plants and trees in an area

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence about parks/trees in your area.
tips: Mention quantity: a few / many / not many
Add a benefit: fresh air / less stress

samples.naturalSimple9: Yes, there are a few parks near my home, and some streets are tree-lined. They’re great for fresh air, especially after a long day. On weekends, they can get a bit crowded.
samples.advancedAcademic9: There are several green spaces in my neighbourhood, and they’re fairly well-maintained. The trees provide shade and improve the overall atmosphere, particularly in summer. It’s a small but valuable part of local life.
samples.fluentStory9: Yes, and I’m glad about that. There’s a small park within walking distance, and in the evenings you can see people jogging or sitting under the trees. It’s the kind of place that helps you unwind without travelling far.

questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 1 • Q3
questions.text: How has your hometown changed over the years?

phrases.t: It used to be…, but now…

examples.t: It used to be quieter, but now it’s more crowded because the population has grown.
Infrastructure has improved a lot, especially roads and public transport.
On the downside, some green areas have disappeared due to construction.

gapFilling.prompt: Over the years, my hometown has ______ rapidly.
Traffic ______ has become worse in the city centre.
Some green areas have disappeared due to ______.

choices: too many cars causing slow traffic

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence comparing the past and present of your hometown.
tips: Add one reason: because / due to
Mention one result: more traffic / better facilities

samples.naturalSimple9: It has changed quite a lot over the years. There are more new buildings and better roads than before. However, it’s also more crowded now, especially in the city centre.
samples.advancedAcademic9: My hometown has experienced noticeable development, particularly in infrastructure and public facilities. While this has improved convenience, it has also led to heavier traffic and a more crowded lifestyle. Overall, it feels more modern but less calm.
samples.fluentStory9: When I was younger, it felt quieter and simpler. Now there’s construction everywhere, new roads, and more busy streets. It’s exciting to see progress, but I do miss the older, calmer atmosphere.

questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 1 • Q4
questions.text: Do you think your hometown is a good place for young people to live?

collocations.t: a good place to settle down

examples.t: It’s budget-friendly and safe, which is good for students and young families.
That said, job opportunities are limited, so many people move to bigger cities.
If someone wants nightlife, they might find it boring.

gapFilling.prompt: My hometown is ______-friendly, so students can manage expenses.
There aren’t many job ______, so people often move away.
If someone wants a vibrant ______ life, a bigger city is better.

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence giving a balanced opinion about young people living in your hometown.

samples.naturalSimple9: It depends on what they want. It’s safe and the cost of living is reasonable, so it’s comfortable for students. That said, job opportunities and entertainment are limited.
samples.advancedAcademic9: Overall, it can be a good option for young people because living costs are manageable and the environment is relatively safe. However, career prospects may be limited compared to larger cities, so ambitious people often relocate. It’s practical, but not highly dynamic.
samples.fluentStory9: For many young people, it’s a nice starting point. You can study, save money, and enjoy a calm lifestyle with friends. But if someone is chasing bigger opportunities, they usually end up moving to a larger city after a few years.

questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 2 • Q1
questions.text: Do you like being around places with a lot of trees or greenery?

examples.t: Definitely. Being surrounded by greenery helps me reduce stress and relax.
I find it refreshing because the air feels cleaner and cooler.
Whenever I can, I choose parks over noisy streets.

gapFilling.prompt: Being around trees has a ______ effect on me.
I go outside to get some ______ air.
Green spaces help me ______ my head.

choices: making you feel better and calmer

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence about how greenery affects you.
tips: Use one feeling word: calm / relaxed

samples.naturalSimple9: Yes, definitely. Being around greenery helps me relax and clear my head. I feel calmer when I spend time in parks or near trees.
samples.advancedAcademic9: Yes, I do. Greenery has a calming effect and it improves my mood, especially after a busy day. I also think fresh air and natural scenery support mental well-being.
samples.fluentStory9: Absolutely. Even a short walk through a tree-lined street makes me feel lighter. When I’m stressed, I go to a quiet green corner and I usually leave feeling refreshed.

questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 2 • Q2
questions.text: Have you ever planted a tree or a flower yourself?

collocations.d: put it in soil so it grows

examples.t: Yes, I’ve planted a few flowers at home, and it was surprisingly satisfying.
I had to water them regularly, but it was nice to see them grow.
It also made my room feel more alive.

gapFilling.prompt: I planted a flower in the ______ and watered it regularly.
It’s nice to see a plant ______ over time.
Taking care of plants can become a daily ______.

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence about planting something.
tips: Add one time phrase: last year / recently

samples.naturalSimple9: Yes, I have. I planted a couple of flowers at home and watered them regularly. It was nice to see them grow little by little.
samples.advancedAcademic9: Yes, I’ve planted flowers before, and I found it surprisingly rewarding. It requires a simple routine, like watering and enough sunlight, but the result is enjoyable. It also makes a home feel more welcoming.
samples.fluentStory9: I have, actually. I planted a small flower in a pot and checked it every morning like a mini project. Watching it grow made me feel proud, even though it was a small thing.

questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 2 • Q3
questions.text: Why do you think people like to grow plants at home?

examples.t: Plants make a home feel cosy and create a calm atmosphere.
Taking care of them gives people a sense of responsibility.
They can also improve mood and reduce stress after work.

gapFilling.prompt: Indoor plants can create a ______ atmosphere.
Looking after plants gives people a sense of ______.
Some people grow plants to ______ their homes.

choices: how many rooms a house has
a duty to take care of something

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence explaining why people grow plants at home.

samples.naturalSimple9: I think it’s because plants make a home feel cosy and calm. They also help people relax after a stressful day. Taking care of them can be enjoyable too.
samples.advancedAcademic9: People often grow plants at home because they improve the indoor environment and create a calmer atmosphere. In addition, caring for plants can reduce stress and build a sense of responsibility. It’s a simple habit with positive effects.
samples.fluentStory9: I think plants change the mood of a room. A few green leaves on a shelf can make a place feel alive and comfortable. Plus, watering them becomes a small routine that helps people slow down and relax.

questions.label: Part 1 • Topic 2 • Q4
questions.text: Are there any famous gardens or parks in your city?

vocab.d: in the middle of the city

examples.t: Yes, there’s a well-known central park, and it’s very popular at weekends.
It’s well-maintained with flowerbeds, walking paths, and a small fountain.
People go there to relax, jog, and spend time with family.

gapFilling.prompt: There’s a ______-known park in the centre of my city.
It’s a popular ______ at weekends.
The park is well-______, so it looks clean.

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence about a famous park/garden in your city.
tips: Name the place (or say “a central park”)

samples.naturalSimple9: Yes, there’s a well-known central park in my city. It’s popular at weekends because it’s clean and family-friendly. People go there to walk, jog, and relax.
samples.advancedAcademic9: Yes, my city has a well-known public park that attracts both residents and tourists. It’s well-maintained, with walking paths, flowerbeds, and open spaces for leisure. It’s a convenient place to unwind without leaving the city.
samples.fluentStory9: Yes, there is. On weekends it feels like everyone ends up there—families, runners, and friends. I like it because it’s peaceful, and a short walk there instantly improves my mood.

cueCard.label: Part 2
cueCard.text:
Describe a place with a lot of trees.
You should say:
Where this place is located
What kinds of trees or plants are there
What people usually do in this place
And explain how you feel when you spend time there

examples.t: It’s a large park on the outskirts of my city with tree-lined paths and fresh air.
People go there to jog, cycle, and sit under the shade to chat.
I feel calm and refreshed because it helps me unwind from daily stress.

gapFilling.prompt: The park is located on the ______ of the city.
There are tree-______ paths that are perfect for walking.
When I go there, I can ______ and recharge.

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence describing the place (location + trees + activity).

samples.naturalSimple9:
Mini-outline:
- Where: a large park near my neighbourhood
- Trees/plants: tall trees, small flowerbeds
- Activities: walking, jogging, sitting
- Feelings: calm and refreshed

Full answer:
I’d like to describe a large park near my neighbourhood that has a lot of trees. It’s located not far from the city centre, but it feels like a peaceful escape from traffic and noise. The park has tall trees that create a lot of shade, as well as small flowerbeds along the paths.

People usually go there to walk, jog, and spend time with friends or family. In the evenings, it’s common to see people sitting on benches and chatting, while others cycle along the trails. Personally, I feel calm and refreshed when I’m there because the fresh air helps me clear my head. Overall, it’s my favourite place to unwind and recharge after a busy day.
samples.advancedAcademic9:
Mini-outline:
- Where: a well-maintained public park on the outskirts
- Trees/plants: pine/poplar, greenery, flowerbeds
- Activities: exercise, leisure, family time
- Feelings: mentally refreshed

Full answer:
I’d like to talk about a well-maintained public park on the outskirts of my city. It’s spacious and carefully designed, with tree-lined paths and open areas where people can relax. In terms of plants, there are pine and poplar trees, plenty of greenery, and neat flowerbeds that make the park look attractive throughout the year.

People usually visit this place for exercise and leisure. Some residents jog or cycle along the trails, while others sit under the trees to read, talk, or simply enjoy the scenery. Families often bring children because it’s safe and comfortable. Personally, I feel mentally refreshed when I spend time there, because it reduces stress and helps me switch off from daily pressure. Overall, it’s an important green space that improves the quality of life in the city.
samples.fluentStory9:
Mini-outline:
- Where: a park I visit after work
- Trees/plants: tall trees, cool shade, green corners
- Activities: walking, thinking, meeting friends
- Feelings: calm + energized

Full answer:
I’d like to describe a park I often visit after work, especially when I need a break. It’s a quiet place a short distance from my home, and the first thing you notice is the tall trees and the cool shade they create. There are also little green corners and flowerbeds along the paths, which make the whole area feel alive.

People use the park in different ways. Some come for a quick jog, others walk slowly and talk, and a few people just sit and watch the day go by. I usually walk there for twenty minutes, breathe the fresh air, and think about my plans. Personally, I always feel calmer and more energized afterwards, because the natural atmosphere helps me reset. For me, it’s a simple place, but it makes a big difference to my mood.

questions.label: Part 3 • Q1
questions.text: Why do people like spending time in natural places?

examples.t: People escape from routine and reduce stress by spending time outdoors.
Fresh air and scenery can improve mental well-being.
As a result, they feel more balanced and refreshed.

gapFilling.prompt: Nature helps people reduce ______ after a busy week.
Many people go outdoors to breathe ______ air.
Natural places offer an escape from daily ______.

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence explaining one reason people enjoy natural places.
tips: Avoid repeating the same word many times

samples.naturalSimple9: People enjoy natural places because they can relax and reduce stress. Fresh air and quiet surroundings help them clear their minds. It’s a simple way to feel better after a busy week.
samples.advancedAcademic9: Natural places offer an escape from routine and noise, which supports mental well-being. In addition, fresh air and pleasant scenery can improve mood and concentration. As a result, people feel more balanced and recharged.
samples.fluentStory9: I think nature gives people a reset button. When you leave traffic and screens behind, your mind slows down and you breathe differently. Even a short walk in a quiet green area can reduce stress and make you feel like yourself again.

questions.label: Part 3 • Q2
questions.text: Do you think it’s important to plant more trees in cities?

examples.t: Trees improve air quality and provide shade during hot summers.
They also reduce urban heat and make streets more comfortable.
So overall, planting trees makes cities more liveable.

gapFilling.prompt: Trees can improve air ______ in crowded cities.
They provide ______ during hot weather.
Planting trees can reduce urban ______.

choices: comfortable and good to live in

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence supporting or opposing planting more trees in cities.

samples.naturalSimple9: Yes, I think it’s important. Trees improve air quality and provide shade, especially in hot weather. They also make cities feel calmer and more comfortable.
samples.advancedAcademic9: Yes, planting more trees in cities is essential for environmental and public health reasons. Trees can reduce air pollution, provide shade, and lower urban temperatures during heatwaves. In the long term, they make cities more sustainable and liveable.
samples.fluentStory9: Definitely. In summer, you can feel the difference between a street with trees and a street without them. Shade, cooler air, and a calmer atmosphere make people want to walk instead of rushing indoors. It’s a small change with a big impact.

questions.label: Part 3 • Q3
questions.text: How can governments encourage people to protect green areas?

examples.t: Governments can raise awareness through schools and public campaigns.
They should enforce laws against illegal cutting and littering.
Incentives like free seedlings can encourage community projects.

gapFilling.prompt: Governments can raise ______ through public campaigns.
They can enforce laws and give ______ for littering.
Offering small ______ can motivate people to protect parks.

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence suggesting one government action to protect green areas.

samples.naturalSimple9: Governments can encourage people by raising awareness through schools and media. They should also enforce laws against littering and illegal cutting. Small incentives, like free seedlings, can help too.
samples.advancedAcademic9: A practical approach is to combine education and enforcement. Governments can raise awareness through public campaigns and school programmes, while also applying strict regulations and meaningful fines. In addition, incentives and community projects can make conservation feel shared and achievable.
samples.fluentStory9: People protect what they value, so governments should help them understand the value first. Clear campaigns, clean parks, and visible rules make a difference. If communities are supported with local planting initiatives and small rewards, people feel involved instead of forced.

questions.label: Part 3 • Q4
questions.text: What differences do you notice between rural and urban environments in terms of greenery?

examples.t: Rural areas usually have widespread greenery like fields and forests.
Cities have planned green spaces such as parks and public gardens.
Overall, rural places feel more open, while cities are more built-up.

gapFilling.prompt: Rural areas often have ______ land and natural scenery.
In cities, green spaces are more ______, like public parks.
Urban areas have ______ space because land prices are high.

choices: how many people/buildings in an area

makingSentences.prompt: Write one sentence comparing greenery in rural vs urban areas.
tips: Use one contrast word: whereas / while
Mention an example for each side

samples.naturalSimple9: In rural areas, greenery is usually more natural and widespread, like fields and forests. Whereas in cities, green areas are often planned, such as parks and public gardens. Cities also have less space, so greenery is more limited.
samples.advancedAcademic9: One key difference is that rural greenery is typically natural and continuous, while urban greenery is planned and restricted by limited space. Cities rely on organised parks and public gardens because land is expensive and density is high. As a result, rural environments often feel more open and breathable.
samples.fluentStory9: When you’re in the countryside, green areas feel endless—fields, trees, and open land. In cities, you usually find greenery in specific places like parks, and it can be crowded. Overall, rural greenery feels natural, while urban greenery feels designed.
